papers.title: A multi-reader multi-case study comparing Breast Cancer Reading Efficiency and Accuracy in Screening with Tomosynthesis versus AI-assisted mammography.
papers.text:
A multi-reader multi-case study comparing Breast Cancer Reading Efficiency and Accuracy in Screening with Tomosynthesis versus AI-assisted mammography..

Objectives

Full-field digital mammography (FFDM) is the standard for breast cancer screening but has reduced sensitivity in dense breasts. Digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) improves cancer detection compared to 2D mammography but is limited by cost and longer reading times. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enhanced mammography has demonstrated improved sensitivity compared to 2D mammography. This study compares AI-enhanced 2D mammography (DM+AI) with DBT in recalling interval breast cancers (IBCs).

Methods

: A multi-reader, multi-case crossover study was conducted using the Emory BrEast Imaging Dataset, which includes paired FFDM and DBT images with biopsy-proven outcomes. Six radiologists reviewed 53 IBC and 53 screen-detected cancer (SDC) cases, with random assignment to DM+AI or DBT, followed by crossover after a washout period. Primary outcomes included recall rate of IBCs. Secondary outcomes included recall rate of SDCs, interpretation time, and subgroup analysis by breast density.

Results

: For IBCs, DM+AI and DBT demonstrated similar recall rates (41.5% vs 40.9%) and detection rates (14.8% vs 11.9%). DM+AI identified more non-invasive (31.5% vs 13.0%) and mass-forming (61.0% vs 21.8%) cancers. For SDCs, recall and detection rates were comparable across modalities. In fatty breasts, recall was higher with DM+AI (91.7% vs 50.0%), while DBT performed better in extremely dense breasts. DM+AI enabled faster interpretation, averaging 24.1 seconds less per case.

Conclusion

: AI-enhanced 2D mammography demonstrated comparable performance to DBT with shorter interpretation times, supporting a stratified screening approach.

Advances in knowledge

This study is the first direct comparison of AI-enhanced mammography and digital breast tomosynthesis for IBC detection.

papers.title: Uncertainty Propagation for Echocardiography Clinical Metric Estimation via Contour Sampling
papers.text: Uncertainty Propagation for Echocardiography Clinical Metric Estimation via Contour Sampling. Echocardiography plays a fundamental role in the extraction of clinical parameters (e.g. left ventricular volume and ejection fraction) required to determine the presence and severity of heart-related conditions. When deploying automated techniques for computing these parameters, uncertainty estimation is highly valuable for assessing their utility. Since clinical parameters are usually derived from segmentation maps, there is no clear path for converting pixel-wise uncertainty values into uncertainty estimates in the downstream clinical metric calculation. In this work, we propose a novel uncertainty estimation method based on contouring rather than segmentation. Our method explicitly predicts contour location uncertainty from which contour samples can be drawn. Finally, the sampled contours can be used to propagate uncertainty to clinical metrics. Our proposed method not only provides accurate uncertainty estimations for the task of contouring but also for the downstream clinical metrics on one public and two private cardiac ultrasound datasets containing a total of 1264 patients. Code is available at: https://github.com/ThierryJudge/contouring-uncertainty.

papers.title: Body composition analysis: Single slice vs. volumetric measures.
papers.text: Body composition analysis: Single slice vs. volumetric measures.. Body composition analysis (BCA) is useful for evaluating nutritional status, general health, and predicting patient outcomes. Computed tomography (CT)-based BCA has become increasingly popular, with research often focusing on single-transaxial-slice measurements at the L3 vertebral level to estimate volumetric tissue properties. This method assumes the same tissue distribution in all transaxial slices across the body, potentially leading to inaccuracies in clinical assessments. This retrospective study investigates the reliability of single-slice BCA compared to volumetric measurements across the torso in a cohort of 237 adults. Using the GA-Net architecture for automatic tissue segmentation, we analyzed tissue distribution at 25 craniocaudal levels. Our results reveal significant variability in tissue distribution, with cross-sectional areas at L3 poorly correlating with 3D tissue volumes. For instance, we observed a visceral adipose tissue (VAT) volume difference of over 2,900 cm<sup>3</sup> between two subjects with similar L3 VAT areas. These findings indicate that single-slice BCA, particularly at L3, is insufficient for accurate body composition analysis. This study underscores the need for more precise, volumetric approaches to BCA, which would enhance the accuracy of clinical assessments, disease prognostication, and treatment planning.

papers.title: P03.01.B AUTOMATED SEGMENTATION OF CEREBRAL ARTERIES ON CONTRAST-ENHANCED MRI PRESENTING INTRACRANIAL TUMORS: AN ALTERNATIVE FOR ANGIOGRAPH TO FACILITATE CLINICAL DIAGNOSTIC ASSESSMENT
papers.text: P03.01.B AUTOMATED SEGMENTATION OF CEREBRAL ARTERIES ON CONTRAST-ENHANCED MRI PRESENTING INTRACRANIAL TUMORS: AN ALTERNATIVE FOR ANGIOGRAPH TO FACILITATE CLINICAL DIAGNOSTIC ASSESSMENT.

papers.title: Geometric Modeling of Hippocampal Tau Deposition: A Surface-Based Framework for Covariate Analysis and Off-Target Contamination Detection
papers.text: Geometric Modeling of Hippocampal Tau Deposition: A Surface-Based Framework for Covariate Analysis and Off-Target Contamination Detection. We introduce a framework combining geometric modeling with disease progression analysis to investigate tau deposition in Alzheimer's disease (AD) using positron emission tomography (PET) data. Focusing on the hippocampus, we construct a principal surface that captures the spatial distribution and morphological changes of tau pathology. By projecting voxels onto this surface, we quantify tau coverage, intensity, and thickness through bidirectional projection distances and interpolated standardized uptake value ratios (SUVR). This low-dimensional embedding preserves spatial specificity while mitigating multiple comparison issues. Covariate effects are analyzed using a two-stage regression model with inverse probability weighting to adjust for signal sparsity and selection bias. Using the SuStaIn model, we identify subtypes and stages of AD, revealing distinct tau dynamics: the limbic-predominant subtype shows age-related nonlinear accumulation in coverage and thickness, whereas the posterior subtype exhibits uniform SUVR increases across disease progression. Model-based predictions show that hippocampal tau deposition follows a structured spatial trajectory expanding bidirectionally with increasing thickness, while subtype differences highlight posterior hippocampal involvement consistent with whole-brain patterns. Finally, directional signal patterns on the principal surface reveal contamination from the choroid plexus, demonstrating the broader applicability of the proposed framework across modalities including amyloid PET.

papers.title: Long-Term Volumetric Increase of a Free Omental Flap in Breast Reconstruction: A Case Report with a Focus on Body Weight Correlation.
papers.text: Long-Term Volumetric Increase of a Free Omental Flap in Breast Reconstruction: A Case Report with a Focus on Body Weight Correlation.. A 53-year-old woman underwent breast reconstruction using a free omental flap following the resection of a phyllodes tumor in the right breast. Postoperative volumetric analysis was retrospectively conducted over 5 years using computed tomography and three-dimensional imaging software. The omental flap demonstrated a 157% increase in volume compared with the immediate postoperative size. A positive correlation (r = 0.93) was observed between body weight and flap volume. Our report is just a single case; therefore, further studies are required to elucidate our hypothesis. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report to describe this association in an omental flap used for breast reconstruction. These findings may support appropriate surgical planning and postoperative follow-up in reconstructive breast surgery.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled early intracranial volumetric response predicts systemic progression-free survival in the phase III CROWN study.
papers.text:
Artificial intelligence-enabled early intracranial volumetric response predicts systemic progression-free survival in the phase III CROWN study..

Background

Manual endpoint assessment is labor-intensive and variable. This study evaluated artificial intelligence (AI)-powered intracranial response assessment and explored imaging prognostic factors in the phase III CROWN trial of advanced treatment-naive anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

Methods

CROWN randomized patients to lorlatinib or crizotinib. Seventy-two with baseline brain metastases (BMs) had brain MRI every 8 weeks. We evaluated an FDA-cleared AI platform, VBrain, for automated lesion-level tracking of BMs and early tumor response (ETR) in relation to systemic progression-free survival (PFS), the primary endpoint of the trial. Progression-free survival was assessed by blinded central review, independent of AI. VBrain assessments were compared with 2 neuroradiologists (R1, R2). Early tumor response at the first on-treatment scan was derived from modified response evaluation criteria in solid tumors (mRECIST) target-lesion diameters and from AI-based all-lesion volumes (AI-ETR). Treatment-neutral Cox models related ETR to systemic PFS; discrimination was assessed using Uno's C and time-dependent AUC(t) with bootstrap uncertainty.

Results

Per mRECIST v1.1, VBrain, R1, and R2 measured 68, 32, and 51 targets, with high concordance ( r  = 0.94). Across 666 time-points, pairwise assessment discordance and time to intracranial progression did not differ between AI and readers. Beyond mRECIST, VBrain tracked 322 tumors. AI-ETR significantly stratified PFS (multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.44, 95% CI, 0.23-0.86), whereas target-diameter ETR was not significant (adjusted HR 0.64, 95% CI, 0.29-1.41). Adding AI-ETR improved prediction vs a clinical base model (Δc-index +0.07; AUC(t) 0.71 vs 0.55).

Conclusions

The AI and human readers reached a high agreement in endpoint evaluations. Volumetric all-BMs ETR outperforming target-only mRECIST offers early prognostic information in advanced ALK-positive NSCLC.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03052608.

papers.title: Towards Reliable Measurement of Cerebellar Morphology: A Comparative Assessment of Segmentation Pipelines.
papers.text: Towards Reliable Measurement of Cerebellar Morphology: A Comparative Assessment of Segmentation Pipelines.. Characterizing cerebellar morphology is fundamental for accurately mapping its structure and function across individuals, yet remains challenging due to its densely foliated architecture. Although multiple automated segmentation pipelines exist, the measurement reproducibility of these tools has not been comprehensively benchmarked. We conducted a systematic assessment of reliability for cerebellar morphology estimates using four commonly used pipelines: one classic parcellation method (CERES), two deep-learning methods (ACAPULCO, DeepCERES), and one voxel-based morphometry toolbox (SUIT). Leveraging the HNU dataset, which provides MRI scans for ten timepoints per individual over a month, we evaluated the test-retest reliability for each of the four pipelines using ReX, an integrative tool for quantifying and optimizing measurement reliability and individual differences. We quantified intra- and inter-individual variability, as well as the Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC), for each pipeline at both global and region-of-interest levels. We used two pools of data: a common dataset of 12 subjects x 5 sessions to benchmark all the pipelines, and method-specific datasets including pools of subjects with 5 valid sessions for each pipeline to assess the generalizability of our findings. Overall, all pipelines yielded highly reliable segmentation volumes (ICC > 0.87). DeepCERES demonstrated the most consistent performance across all metrics and subject pools, while SUIT achieved the highest ICC on the common dataset but showed decreased reliability when evaluated on a larger subject pool. Importantly, our analysis highlighted substantial heterogeneity in reliability across lobules for each method. Lobule X consistently showed reduced reliability whereas lobules I-V, VI, Crus I, IX, and VIIIB were reliably estimated across all pipelines. While all pipelines demonstrated strong reliability, DeepCERES showed the most robust and consistent performance overall. Substantial lobule-specific variability and method-dependent failure rates underscore the need for reliability-aware pipeline selection to optimize cerebellar morphology estimation in research.

papers.title: Quantifying "Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus"-like Brain Morphometry patterns in an Alzheimer's Disease Cohort.
papers.text:
Quantifying "Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus"-like Brain Morphometry patterns in an Alzheimer's Disease Cohort..

Background and purpose

Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is largely underdiagnosed. It is a potentially treatable contributor to cognitive decline, and cognitive improvement may occur even with comorbid Alzheimer's disease. However, iNPH-related imaging features can overlap with age-related and neurodegenerative atrophy, making differentiation difficult. Automated morphometric profiling of NPH-like patterns in biomarker-defined Alzheimer's disease cohorts has not been systematically explored. This pilot study aimed to quantify iNPH-like brain morphometry in an Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort using deep-learning-based morphometry and automated callosal angle measurement.

Materials and methods

We included N=30 amyloid-negative reference iNPH patients and N=1003 ADNI participants with structural T1-weighted MRI and CSF biomarkers. Age- and sex-adjusted volumetric z-scores were obtained using a deep-learning-based morphometry algorithm. We derived an iNPH morphometric profile using principal component analysis and Gaussian modeling of the reference iNPH cohort and applied it to the ADNI participants to compute individual iNPH similarity scores. We also automated callosal angle measurement for further clinical representation. We compared scores across cognitive stages and biological Alzheimer's disease groups and evaluated against expert Radscale review.

Results

iNPH-like morphometry increased with cognitive impairment, with mean differences of 0.03 between cognitively normal and mild cognitive impairment (p=0.06), 0.06 between mild cognitive impairment and dementia (p<0.001), and 0.09 between cognitively normal and dementia groups (p<0.001). Among cognitively impaired participants, scores were higher in biologically-defined Alzheimer's disease patients than biologically-defined non-Alzheimer's disease patients (mean difference=0.08, p<0.001). The iNPH similarity score correlated most strongly with ventricular enlargement features. Automated callosal angle measurements showed high agreement with expert ratings (Gwet's AC1 = 0.939) and angles below 90° occurred in 1.5% of ADNI participants.

Conclusions

Automated normative morphometric profiling and callosal angle quantification identified heterogeneous iNPH-like structural patterns in the ADNI cohort. These tools provide a scalable approach for characterizing iNPH-like imaging features in dementia cohorts where identifying a potentially treatable contributor to cognitive impairment remains relevant. Further clinical validation remains necessary.

papers.title: Diagnostic accuracy of 3D MRI rendering techniques for evaluation of hourglass-like constrictions in Parsonage-Turner syndrome.
papers.text: Diagnostic accuracy of 3D MRI rendering techniques for evaluation of hourglass-like constrictions in Parsonage-Turner syndrome.. To evaluate inter-reader agreement and diagnostic accuracy of curved multiplanar reformatting (cMPR) and maximum intensity projection (MIP) techniques for detecting hourglass-like constrictions (HGCs). Thirty brachial plexus 3-Tesla, 3D, 1-mm isotropic MR neurography (MRN) datasets (10 patients without and 20 patients with Parsonage-Turner syndrome (PTS) affecting the suprascapular nerve (SSN)) were retrospectively analyzed by four musculoskeletal radiology fellows for the number and severity of HGCs using both post-processing views in a randomized, blinded fashion. An experienced, attending radiologist served as the reference standard. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using Gwet's AC1 and intraclass correlation (ICC). Image interpretation time was compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Inter-reader agreement for HGC presence was substantial to almost perfect among fellows (cMPR AC1 = 0.7, MIP AC1 = 0.67) and when compared to the attending (cMPR AC1 = 0.67-0.83, MIP AC1 = 0.63-0.83). Agreement for severe HGC count was substantial to almost perfect (fellows: cMPR ICC = 0.65, MIP ICC = 0.79; vs. attending: ICC = 0.62-0.83, MIP ICC = 0.69-0.88), but poor to fair for mild HGCs (fellows: cMPR ICC = 0.23, MIP ICC = 0.26; vs. attending: ICC = 0-0.21, MIP ICC = 0-0.09). Sensitivity to HGC presence was excellent (cMPR, 85-100%; MIP, 90-100%), though specificity (cMPR, 50-100%; MIP, 40-90%) and diagnostic accuracy (cMPR, 80-90%; MIP, 76-90%) varied. The MIP method required significantly less interpretation time than cMPR (median: 33 vs. 104 s, p < 0.001). High inter-reader agreement and sensitivity but variable specificity for HGC detection suggest both techniques are viable tools for MRN, with cMPR better suited for detailed HGC evaluation and MIP for initial screening.

papers.title: MRI-based virtual radiographs of the pelvis for assessment of acetabular morphology.
papers.text:
MRI-based virtual radiographs of the pelvis for assessment of acetabular morphology..

Objectives

We generated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based virtual radiographs (VRs) from hips with/without intra-articular contrast and compared them with conventional anteroposterior pelvic radiographs (CR) regarding measurement bias, interobserver and intraobserver agreement, and diagnosis of acetabular deformities; we also assessed hip deformity prevalence on VR in asymptomatic participants.

Materials and methods

Retrospective study of 50 patients (100 hips; mean age 34 years) with femoroacetabular impingement or hip dysplasia undergoing CR and unilateral magnetic resonance arthrography. Additionally, 53 asymptomatic participants underwent noncontrast MRI. Segmentation of the osseous pelvis was performed on T1-weighted volume interpolated breathhold examination (VIBE) Dixon MRI using 3D nnU-Net, pseudo-computed tomography generation, and cone-beam projection to generate VR. Acetabular coverage (lateral center edge angle (LCE), acetabular index (AI), anterior/posterior coverage, extrusion index (EI)), and acetabular version were compared between CR and VR. Interobserver agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and κ statistics; bias with Bland-Altman analysis.

Results

Interobserver agreement for VR ranged from moderate to almost perfect (ICC/κ 0.60-0.94), except for the AI. LCE showed no significant bias with ( - 0.2° ± 2.5, p = 0.663) or without contrast ( - 0.2° ± 2.2, p = 0.530). Systematic differences occurred for AI, EI, anterior/posterior coverage, and ischial spine sign; 57-75% of discrepancies were within CR interobserver variation. Diagnostic classification showed substantial agreement between CR and VR (κ = 0.62), comparable to CR interobserver agreement (κ = 0.70). In asymptomatic participants, 13% had acetabular dysplasia, 68% normal coverage, and 19% overcoverage.

Conclusion

MRI-based VR provides acetabular morphology assessment comparable to CR and enables radiation-free evaluation in symptomatic patients and asymptomatic populations.

Key points

Question Can MRI-based virtual radiographs reproduce conventional radiographic measurements of acetabular morphology, enabling radiation-free two-dimensional assessment in symptomatic patients and asymptomatic populations? Findings The lateral center-edge angle showed no significant bias between virtual and conventional radiographs; diagnostic classification of acetabular deformities agreed substantially (κ = 0.62), comparable to conventional radiograph interobserver agreement. Relevance Statement MRI-derived virtual radiographs can provide acetabular measurements comparable to conventional radiographs without ionizing radiation, supporting integration into three-dimensional surgical planning and enabling assessment in young patients and population-based cohorts where repeated radiographs are undesirable.

papers.title: Systolic pressure gradient across myocardial bridge mediates the effect of bridge depth on clinical symptoms.
papers.text: Systolic pressure gradient across myocardial bridge mediates the effect of bridge depth on clinical symptoms.. The relationship between myocardial bridging (MB) morphology and function and the pathways to clinical symptoms remained unclear. This study investigated the association between delta coronary computed tomographic angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (ΔCT-FFR) and angina-equivalent symptoms in left anterior descending MB without coronary atherosclerosis using photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT). This retrospective cohort included 180 patients with deep MB (depth > 2 mm) and no plaques. All underwent PCD-CT angiography. CT-FFR was computed by machine learning; systolic (ΔCT-FFRsys) and diastolic (ΔCT-FFRdia) trans-bridge pressure gradients were derived. MB depth and length were measured. Associations with symptoms were assessed by logistic regression and mediation analysis. Symptomatic patients (n = 81) had greater depth (median 3.30 mm vs. 2.45 mm), longer length (mean 36.06 mm vs. 26.10 mm), higher ΔCT-FFRsys (3.81% vs. 1.62%) and ΔCT-FFRdia (3.45% vs. 2.15%) than asymptomatic patients (n = 99) (all p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis identified depth (OR = 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.46, p = 0.001) and ΔCT-FFRsys (OR = 1.16, 95% CI: 1.05-1.27, p = 0.002) as independent predictors. Mediation analysis indicated that ΔCT-FFRsys significantly mediated the effect of depth on symptoms (indirect effect = 0.1881, 95% CI: 0.1023-0.2897). MB depth and ΔCT-FFRsys were independent risk factors for symptoms, and ΔCT-FFRsys appeared to mediate the morphological-clinical symptoms link. These findings suggested that integrated assessment, particularly ΔCT-FFRsys, might be a new non-invasive imaging biomarker for clinically identify symptomatic MB and understand its potential pathogenic mechanisms. Question The precise relationship between myocardial bridging morphological and functional features and clinical symptoms, and whether underlying key mediating factors exist, remains currently incompletely determined. Findings Depth, length, and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient of myocardial bridging independently predicted symptoms, with the gradient significantly mediating the relationship between morphology and clinical presentation. Clinical relevance Noninvasive assessment of depth and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient can assist in identifying patients with symptomatic myocardial bridging, serving as potential imaging biomarkers and providing insights into the underlying pathophysiology of symptom presentation.

papers.title: Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening Using CT-Derived Volumetric Bone Mineral Density Reference Curves.
papers.text: Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening Using CT-Derived Volumetric Bone Mineral Density Reference Curves.. Computed tomography (CT) scans are a widely available yet underused resource that can be leveraged for opportunistic osteoporosis screening. This study aimed to develop sex- and site-specific reference curves for volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) to define dual X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-anchored percentile thresholds for osteoporosis classification, and to evaluate whether these thresholds identified individuals who subsequently sustain a major osteoporotic fracture (MOF). A retrospective cohort of 4,418 clinical CT scans was analyzed, including a subset of 1,088 scans with corresponding DXA imaging within one year. MOF incidence and timing following CT were obtained from linked administrative health data. CT images were segmented with deep learning models to extract the first lumbar vertebra (L1) and femoral neck from which vBMDs were assessed using internal calibration. Sex-specific vBMD centile curves were generated for each region using Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape. A receiver operating characteristic analysis with the Youden index defined percentile thresholds that aligned with DXA-defined osteoporosis. Clinical relevance was assessed by determining the proportion of participants classified as osteoporotic by the CT-derived percentile thresholds who subsequently sustained a MOF, and by evaluating the association between CT-defined osteoporosis and time to incident fracture using Cox proportional hazards models. The cohort included 2,368 males and 2,050 females. At the vertebral body, 66.3% (n=67) of female and 41.9% (n=26) of male fracture cases had vBMD values below the CT-defined osteoporosis threshold, consistent with osteoporosis. Among these, 44.8% (n=30) of females and 76.9% (n=20) of males had not undergone DXA screening. Individuals classified as osteoporotic based on CT-derived thresholds had up to 2.86 times higher risk of sustaining an MOF across all vertebral sites in both sexes. These findings indicate that CT-derived vBMD percentile thresholds offer clinically meaningful cut-points for opportunistic screening and support their use as a diagnostic flag for further evaluation.

papers.title: Adaptive Squeeze-and-Shrink Image Denoising for Improving Deep Detection of Cerebral Microbleeds.
papers.text: Adaptive Squeeze-and-Shrink Image Denoising for Improving Deep Detection of Cerebral Microbleeds.. Deep learning for medical image analysis requires large quantities of high-quality imaging data for training purposes, which could be often less available due to existence of heavy noise in particular imaging modalities. This issue is especially obvious in cerebral microbleed (CMB) detection, since CMBs are more discernable on long echo time (TE) susceptibility weighted imaging (SWI) data, which are unfortunately much noisier than those with shorter TE. In this paper we present an effective unsupervised image denoising scheme with application to boosting the performance of deep learning based CMB detection. The proposed content-adaptive denoising technique uses the log-determinant of covariance matrices formed by highly correlated image contents retrieved from the input itself to implicitly and efficiently exploit sparsity in PCA domain. The numerical solution to the corresponding optimization problem comes down to an adaptive squeeze-and-shrink (ASAS) operation on the underlying PCA coefficients. Obviously, the ASAS denoising does not rely on any external dataset and could be better fit the input image data. Experiments on medical image datasets with synthetic Gaussian white noise demonstrate that the proposed ASAS scheme is highly competitive among state-of-the-art sparsity based approaches as well as deep learning based method. When applied to the deep learning based CMB detection on the real-world TE3 SWI dataset, the proposed ASAS denoising could improve the precision by 18.03%, sensitivity by 7.64%, and increase the correlation between counts of ground truth and automated detection by 19.87%.

papers.title: CAVASS-DL: An Enhanced Computer-Assisted Visualization and Analysis Software System by Integrating Deep Learning Segmentation Models.
papers.text: CAVASS-DL: An Enhanced Computer-Assisted Visualization and Analysis Software System by Integrating Deep Learning Segmentation Models.. Segmentation in medical images plays a crucial first step for the quantitative analysis of organs of interest and disease conditions that may affect them. In the 2000s, we released an open-source medical image processing and analysis software system called CAVASS (Computer-Assisted Visualization and Analysis Software System), whose lineage goes back to 1980 as the first software for medical image processing. CAVASS supports multiple types of medical images and numerous usage scenarios/use cases. To allow ready access to advanced deep learning models within the easy-to-use graphical user interface (GUI) of CAVASS to greatly facilitate ground truth segmentation generation and production mode image segmentation, we created an enhanced version of CAVASS, called CAVASS-DL, by integrating the Segment Anything Model (SAM) within our software, which can extract and fuse the features from images and interactive prompts to enhance the segmentation performance. Firstly, we modified the GUI to enable intuitive region-of-interest (ROI) prompting via bounding boxes. Secondly, we implemented and trained the SAM network using PyTorch platform. Lastly, we bundled the SAM network as a standalone executable interface for CAVASS. The illustrative and quantitative results on 20 dynamic MRI scans of neck and thorax demonstrate that our approach achieves high accuracy and efficiency for semi-automatic anatomy object segmentation via CAVASS-DL in a convenient manner.

papers.title: Multi-classification of Brain Tumor MRI images using Convoluted Neural Network (CNN) based approach
papers.text: Multi-classification of Brain Tumor MRI images using Convoluted Neural Network (CNN) based approach. Abstract A brain tumor is considered a fatal condition, and a wrong diagnosis of the type and stage of the brain tumor will reduce the patient’s survival rate. Many malignancies, according to the World Health Organization (WHO), can be treated if detected early. Inspecting MRI scans is a convenient way of identifying brain tumors, but it is time consuming and can lead to human errors due to the enormous amount of data. To address this issue, different deep learning methods are used in literature for identification and categorization of various types of cancers, allowing doctors to plan treatment. In this study, we have proposed a model that uses a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for the classification of brain tumors into Glioma, Meningioma, Pituitary and absentia (no tumor or normal condition). CNN is a deep learning algorithm built primarily for tasks that require object recognition, such as picture categorization, detection, and segmentation. The suggested model incorporates 7 convolutional layers with different kernel sizes, and ReLU is utilized as an activation function. Model was trained and tested on a publicly available dataset on Kaggle. The dataset consists of 7023 images, 5712 images for training and 1311 for testing. Using our simple architecture without any pre-trained model, we have achieved a training accuracy of 99.71%, a validation accuracy of 96.06% and a test accuracy of 96.10%. These results significantly demonstrate robustness of the proposed model and shows promising performance for computer-aided diagnosis. The model outperformed the existing comparative models for automated brain tumour detection and warrants further clinical validation.

papers.title: A web modular AI interface for brain tumor MRI classification using deep learning models.
papers.text: A web modular AI interface for brain tumor MRI classification using deep learning models.. In order to improve patient outcomes and treatment processes, early and precise diagnosis of brain tumors is crucial. Despite the strong performance shown by deep learning models in classifying brain tumors from MRI scans, integrating these models into user-friendly clinical workflows remains challenging. This study presents a web-based AI platform designed for brain tumor classification using MRI images. The platform enables users to upload MRI scans, apply standardized preprocessing, select between different deep learning models, and receive real-time predictions. A custom convolutional neural network (CNN), pretrained VGG19, and pretrained Xception were evaluated using a publicly available T1-weighted contrast-enhanced brain MRI dataset of approximately 7,000 images across four classes: glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, and no tumor. The dataset lacks patient demographic and clinical metadata, limiting assessment of clinical generalizability. The models achieved test accuracies of 96.03%, 98%, and 96%, respectively, with VGG19 demonstrating the best performance. The study is limited by the use of a single public, slice-based dataset and the absence of external clinical validation; future work will focus on multi-sequence MRI and independent clinical cohorts.

papers.title: Interpretable Deep Learning Models for Breast Cancer Diagnosis Using Medical Imaging
papers.text: Interpretable Deep Learning Models for Breast Cancer Diagnosis Using Medical Imaging. Deep learning shows promise for breast cancer diagnosis, but limited interpretability hinders clinical adoption. We benchmark ten ImageNet-pretrained models (ResNet50, VGG19, InceptionV3, DenseNet121, Xception, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet, ConvNeXt, ViT, and Swin Transformer) for benign-versus-malignant classification on the BreakHis histopathology dataset using a patient-level split, and explain their predictions with Grad-CAM, LIME, Integrated Gradients, and LRP. DenseNet121 performed best, with 99.4% test accuracy and an AUC-ROC of 0.999, and significantly outperformed all other models (p < 0.001). Transformer-based models trailed the CNNs. The explanations consistently highlighted nuclei-rich and glandular regions of diagnostic relevance. Combining transfer learning with explainable AI can thus yield accurate, interpretable tools for breast cancer diagnosis.
